name: Session
tagline: Pomodoro focus timer for mindful productivity.
description:
Session is a Pomodoro-style focus timer for Mac, iPhone, and iPad that combines timed work intervals with distraction blocking and progress review. Begin by naming the focus, work for the selected session, and use the end-of-session prompt to reflect on what happened instead of treating every timer as identical.

On the Mac, it can block chosen applications and websites while a focus period runs, then restore access when it ends. This makes it useful for work that benefits from both a time boundary and a temporary reduction in obvious diversions.

Session also syncs progress through its own service across Apple devices. That convenience means the app is more than an isolated local timer, so it is worth reviewing the current subscription, data, and account terms before adopting it as a long-running personal record.

## Features

- Start focused work sessions built around a 25-minute default rhythm, then adapt the practice to the task at hand.
- Block selected Mac apps and websites during a session, with website support for Safari, Chrome, Brave, and Microsoft Edge according to the developer.
- Restore the blocked items when the session ends so the boundary is temporary rather than a permanent configuration change.
- Track progress, prompt for a short reflection after a session, and review the day’s work later.
- Sync progress among the current Mac, iPhone, and iPad apps through Session’s service.
- Update and restore a Slack status automatically during a focus session when the current Pro integration is configured.

## Where it fits

Session fits people who want a focus timer to actively protect attention and provide a record for reflection. It is more structured than a bare Pomodoro timer but lighter than a full task-management suite.

The web blocker should be tested with the browsers and work sites you actually use, and sync means your data is backed up on the provider’s servers. A simpler local timer may be preferable if blocking, cross-device history, or a subscription is not important.
